elements.element: The liability cap is mutual.
elements.evidence: Section 21.1 applies the cap to “each Party” and expressly states that the cap is mutual.

elements.element: One cap limb is the fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim.
elements.evidence: Section 21.1 uses “the fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim” as limb (a).

elements.element: One cap limb is USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Section 21.1 specifies “USD 1,000,000” as limb (b).

elements.element: The cap equals the greater of the 12-month fees limb and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Section 21.1 expressly applies “the greater of” limbs (a) and (b).

elements.element: Indirect damages are excluded mutually.
elements.evidence: Subject to Excluded Claims, Section 21.2 states that “neither Party” is liable for indirect damages.

elements.element: Consequential damages are excluded mutually.
elements.evidence: Subject to Excluded Claims, Section 21.2 states that “neither Party” is liable for consequential damages.

elements.element: Liability for breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped for either Party.
elements.evidence: A Party’s breach of confidentiality obligations is an Excluded Claim, and Section 21.1 exempts Excluded Claims from the cap.

elements.evidence: A Party’s breach of data-protection obligations is an Excluded Claim, and Section 21.1 exempts Excluded Claims from the cap.

elements.element: Liability for gross negligence is uncapped for either Party.

result.reason: The operative language fully implements the preferred position, including the greater-of cap, mutual damages exclusion, all required uncapped carve-outs, and treatment of Customer payment obligations. Assessed independently, the fallback is not fully satisfied because its specified cap equals 12 months’ fees, whereas the rendered cap includes a USD 1,000,000 floor. The changes are confined to the cap formula and payment-obligation treatment needed for the preferred position, and unrelated terms remain effective. Drafting quality is reduced because lowercase “fees” is undefined and sits alongside a materially narrower defined term “Fees,” creating avoidable interpretive ambiguity over the intended fee base.
